### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **47** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine-count-aggregate.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**73** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5d7cfe6a5ea3c31301f57af52ab72f3f86e593ce`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine-count-aggregate.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 79 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5d7cfe6a5ea3c31301f57af52ab72f3f86e593ce` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4a96d7d3e16892cef4cea15f58207c205c6f76b6` — the merge of head `9ebb8ae8eed4dc557261acdf1ed403b360b68ede` into base `5d7cfe6a5ea3c31301f57af52ab72f3f86e593ce`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4a96d7d3e16892cef4cea15f58207c205c6f76b6 && git checkout 4a96d7d3e16892cef4cea15f58207c205c6f76b6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5d7cfe6a5ea3c31301f57af52ab72f3f86e593ce 9ebb8ae8eed4dc557261acdf1ed403b360b68ede && git checkout -B drift-repro 5d7cfe6a5ea3c31301f57af52ab72f3f86e593ce && git merge --no-ff 9ebb8ae8eed4dc557261acdf1ed403b360b68ede

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5d7cfe6a5ea3c31301f57af52ab72f3f86e593ce
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5d7cfe6a5ea3c31301f57af52ab72f3f86e593ce` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9ebb8ae8eed4dc557261acdf1ed403b360b68ede`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/internal-field-evaluation-guard.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-count-aggregate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/host-engine.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json, packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json, packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.internal-field-evaluation.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.data-door-internal-field-delegation.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/internal-field-evaluation-guard.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/internal-fields.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-data-door-internal-field-positions.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-internal-field-evaluate-positions.dogfood.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution-calldata-aggregate-internal-field.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/credential-evaluation-guard.ts, packages/objectql/src/secret-fields.ts (`collectInternalReadFields`), packages/core/src/utils/internal-write-response.ts (`collectInternalWriteResponseFields`), packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts and packages/objectql/src/plugin.step2.test.ts (the `registerProtocol` option), packages/metadata-protocol/src/plugin.ts (the engine the door is built over), packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts (the verifier's context)

Face: `--paths` on the PR's file list derives the schema face (hit: `packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts`); the `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` line on the PR body and the changeset adds the narrowing face, whose floor is every non-prose path of the diff, listed above before the `+`. Inputs: the PR body and file list, the commit message, the changeset, the net diff against merge-base `7fa9873f38f7` (24 files, +1276 −492), the claim on the seat mailbox #28284 (comment 6568148765), the contract review on #28875 (record 6567682353) the declaration follows, and the check-runs on the head. The prose faces (`.changeset/engine-internal-field-evaluation-gate.md`, `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`, `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`) are the lane seat's ACCEPT, read here only for the declaration lines and the disclosure rule.

Check-runs on the head, read until every run completed: 70 runs, 58 `success`, 12 `skipped`, 0 failed, 0 in progress. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (8 shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` (16 shards), `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` concluded `success`; `Lint UI` is `skipped` (no `ui/**` path in the diff), and every other `skipped` run is an opt-in, schedule-gated or paths-filtered job (`18.x upgrade harness`, `Packed-tarball smoke`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the dogfood shard matrix, `UI Published Artifacts`).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The refusal has one definition, and it is the engine's — right.** `packages/objectql/src/internal-field-evaluation-guard.ts` is the only walk over the positions (filter, including a relation hop and a `$field` comparand; sort; group key; aggregation operand; an aggregation's own filter; the same positions at every `expand` level, each against its own target). `ObjectQL#assertNoInternalFieldEvaluated` serves it as the `QueryEvaluationGate` member; `find`, `findOne`, `count` and `aggregate` apply it on the read path for every caller but a system context, before the credential guard and before any search expansion, token resolution, middleware or driver. The data door (`protocol-query-validation.ts#assertNoInternalFieldEvaluated`), the HTTP MCP data bridge (`action-execution.ts#callData`, `query` and `aggregate` arms) and the stdio MCP bridge all reach that one definition; the door's and the stdio bridge's own copies are deleted, and nothing in the diff restates the rule. Verified against the tree, not the body.
2. **The moved door answers are unchanged — right.** The guard's filter-read collector is the door's (`protocol.ts#collectFilterReads`, kept there for its other users) line for line; the sort and group-key name readers, the refusal sentence and the envelope (`INVALID_FIELD`, 400, `object`, `field`, `fields`, `param`) are the door's verbatim; the two flag readers (`collectInternalReadFields` in objectql, `collectInternalWriteResponseFields` in core) select the same `internal === true` set; the "no usable field map" early return matches the door's `resolveQueryFields`. The door's relation-target exposure question (`refuseUnservedRelationTarget`) rides the gate's `beforeRelationTarget` hook at each hop, before the hop's fields are judged, so the order of refusals is the one the door gave. The 50-case position matrix moved from metadata-protocol to objectql with its cases unchanged and the engine-double ledger re-pointed.
3. **The published `objectql` slot contract widens by one required member — right, and it is the safe shape.** `IObjectQLEngine` is required-by-default (its own docblock: only three members are optional by ruling), so every implementer of the published type must carry `assertNoInternalFieldEvaluated`; `ObjectQL implements IObjectQLEngine` is the verification. No other implementer of the type exists in this repo, objectui or hotcrm. `MetadataHostEngine` (the door's narrower host type) marks it optional, as it marks `transaction`, and the door's own exposure question is asked at every hop whichever engine it is built over (pinned). Accepted: the one engine the protocol is built over in production is the kernel's `objectql` service, whose contract now requires the member; the optional mark is a test-double allowance, and the reasoning is in the seat's private notes.
4. **Non-internal fields and the faces that already had a protocol service: behaviour-preserving — right.** The guard returns without judging when the object declares no flagged field; controls on every face (engine, door, callData with and without a protocol, stdio, HTTP MCP, dogfood) pin ordinary fields served in every position and the flagged column still absent from rows. The REST door's answers are the moved matrix's, unchanged.
5. **The system-context exemption is the existing ADR-0100 line — right.** `rejectInternalFieldEvaluation` skips exactly `context.isSystem === true`, read through the same `mergeReadContext` seam as the credential guard; a context-less call is judged like any non-system caller (pinned). The doors (REST `findData`, `callData` both arms) ask the member for every caller, system included, so a door's answer does not depend on who is asking. Every server lookup in the tree that matches on a flagged column is named in the census row 18e and the moved `internal-fields.test.ts` pins now read as the real verifier does.
6. **Spec stays logic-free — right.** `objectql-engine.ts` gains three interfaces and one `extends`; no runtime code in `packages/spec`. API-surface and export-origin snapshots regenerated and committed (Human Minimum 6).

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — right.** The diff narrows the engine's read-path accept set (a declared capability of the engine is refused for non-system callers) and widens a published public surface (the `objectql` slot contract gains a member and three exported types). AGENTS.md rule 3 admits one arm; the closed pair's narrowing arm carries the breaking signal, and the #28875 reading (record 6567682353) and `record-recognisers.mjs` ("`yes (narrowing)` included: a diff that widens and narrows owes the narrowing face") name this exact form. The claim on #28284 expected `no`; the dev measured and declared, as the claim said it would, and the PR body states the reason.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` — right.** Nothing an author writes is added, refused, tombstoned or re-meant; the `internal: true` key is read as before. All five packages `patch` — right under ruling A on #25105: the level follows the protocol kind alone, and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` requires every entry of a `none` changeset to be `patch`. The order's "spec minor" is superseded by that ruling; the changeset says so.
- **BREAKING carriers — present.** The changeset carries the `**BREAKING**` banner, the FROM → TO pair and the one-line remedy; the PR title and the changeset summary carry the conventional-commit `!`, consistent with the narrowing arm (no gate requires the `!` beside the arm; it is not a defect).
- **ADR-0087 — not owed, correctly stated.** No authorable key, export rename or config field moves, so there is no migration to prescribe; the changeset holds exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with both declaration lines beside it, the form `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` reads. `Check Changeset` (which runs both gates) is `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `os-project-manager`, not the fleet bot; read before landing.
- **Dev deviation: the declaration arm differs from the claim's expectation** — answered in ② (right).
- **Dev deviation: `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` for a new published type** — answered in ② (right under ruling A).
- **Dev deviation: the door's host type marks the new member optional** — answered in ① item 3 (accepted, with the reasoning in the private notes).
- **Dev flag: the dogfood battery ran before the last fixup** — the fixup touched a runtime test's null guard, a metadata-protocol test double, the engine-double ledger and the spec snapshots, none of which the battery reads; the head's `Dogfood Regression Gate` check is `success`, so the head is covered.
- **Cross-organization caller class: NOT MEASURED** (the showcase cannot mint a second organization). The refusal reads only the object's declared schema and the `isSystem` mark, before any middleware injects organization, sharing or row-level filters, so by construction its answer cannot vary by organization. The code reading is sufficient to land; a second-organization dogfood row is a follow-up once a fixture can build one, not a landing condition.
- **Out of scope (dev-flagged):** a related position outside this PR's acceptance is recorded in the seat's private notes with a recommendation that it be its own item; it does not move this verdict.
- **Overlap:** #28997 shares no file with this PR (confirmed from its file list: metadata redaction, metadata manager, connector credential redaction, their tests and changeset). #28850 and #28731 (open) touch `protocol.ts` in other regions, no shared symbol; #28887 and #28764 are closed. The branch merges cleanly onto current `main` per the PR; nothing here contradicts it.
- **Disclosure rule:** the PR body, the commit message and the changeset say what is hardened and how behaviour changes, in product words; none carries a reproduction, a request sequence, a caller matrix or a prior-state description, and the maintainer quick-read's "为什么改" line is exactly the fixed sentence. Held.
- **Governed surfaces:** none in the file list; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`.
- **Should-fix (doc accuracy, not a verdict mover):** `packages/objectql/src/credential-evaluation-guard.ts`'s header docblock still describes where the `internal: true` evaluate refusal lives and why; after this PR that paragraph is stale and should point at `internal-field-evaluation-guard.ts`.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the published spec on `main`: `IObjectQLEngine` is the one contract between the kernel's `objectql` slot and every consumer, and the `internal: true` flag is defined there as "never returned on a generic data exit". This change makes the engine itself keep that promise in every position that would otherwise evaluate the field, with one definition, and it takes no declared capability away from a consumer that the spec ever promised: a system context keeps its server-side match, every other caller keeps every ordinary field, and the refusal a caller meets is the data door's own, on every face.

1. **`QueryEvaluationGate` against its first consumers.** The member's signature (`object`, a query slice whose every member is optional, an options bag with one hook) is exactly what the door, `callData` and the engine's own read path need, and nothing more; the hook gives a door its "ask my own question first at each hop" without the gate learning about exposure. Required on `IObjectQLEngine` is the contract's default and the shape that makes implementers fail closed at compile time; the host-type optional mark is confined to the door's narrower type. Holds.
2. **Position coverage against the door's matrix.** The 50 moved cases and the 29 new engine cases cover every position the door judged, plus the engine-path-only cases (context-less caller, system caller served with the column still withheld, the hop hook's throw winning). Holds.
3. **Ordering.** The guard runs before the credential guard, so a flagged column that is also credential-typed answers in the door's words on every face; before search expansion and middleware, so server-authored filters are never judged. Holds.
4. **Cost.** One registry read per object per level and a linear walk of the caller's own query; no driver call, no new allocation on the hot path beyond the read set. Holds.
5. **Evidence.** Red first measured by the dev on the base sources; one-shot ablation of the single call line reds 24 objectql pins and 28 dogfood rows, with the restore proven (blob == HEAD, empty diff, present-mode preflight); six package suites, `test:repo` on spec/objectql/runtime, the dogfood battery under the lock (382 files, 3172 tests) and 118/118 derived gates exit 0 per the PR; the head's check-runs are read above.

Findings: one should-fix (the stale docblock in ③). No must-fix.
